problem_statement: The paper frames portfolio optimization as the task of selecting the best mix of assets to maximize return, minimize risk, or balance both under changing market conditions. It also emphasizes that portfolio management involves dynamic decision-making with constraints such as transaction costs, liquidity, taxes, and limited resources.
problem_statement_quotes: Portfolio optimization has always been a challenging proposition in finance and manage- ment. Portfolio optimization facilitates in selection of portfolios in a volatile market situ- ation.

The portfolio management tech- niques hence require better allocation of stock to maximize return while keeping the risk low. Portfolio management and optimization have always been a challenging problem
The main contribution of this paper is that it presents a brief review of clas- sical and intelligent approaches that can be employed for portfolio optimization.
Portfolio optimization is the process of selecting the best combination of assets based on pre-defined objectives. The objectives could be maximization of return or minimization of risk, or both.
classical_baseline: The paper treats classical portfolio optimization as the established set of statistical approaches, especially mean-variance, variance with skewness, mean-absolute deviation, minimax, lower partial moments, Value-at-Risk, and Conditional Value-at-Risk. It also mentions traditional methods such as hidden Markov models, efficient frontier, and Monte Carlo simulation.
classical_baseline_quotes: Almost all the classical approaches like mean-variance Markowitz and Todd (2000), variance with skewness Samuelson (1975), mean absolute deviation Konno and Yamazaki (1991); Konno and Koshizuka (2005), minimax Cai et al. (2004) Li et al. (2019), and lower partial moments Nawrocki (1992) mentioned in Table 5 are based on asset and cardinality constraints
Value-at-Risk (VaR) Dowd (2007)Holton (2003)Jorion (2007) is a measure of, how the market value of an asset is likely to reduce over a period of time under certain market conditions.

Some of the traditional techniques like hidden markov model Rabiner and Juang (1986), efficient frontier Best and Hlouskova (2000), and monte carlo simulation Pedersen (2014) are other popular classical approaches used in portfolio optimization.
classical_difficulty: The paper says the problem is hard classically because market factors and constraints change dynamically, and because solving for the right asset distribution requires high computation power in a timely manner. It also notes that mean-variance becomes difficult for large-scale problems because covariance computation is challenging, and that some classical methods are misleading or non-convex under non-normal or discrete distributions.
classical_difficulty_quotes: Some of the key factors which make it an area of interest includes (i) dynamically changing market factors (ii) dynamically changing constraints like regu- larity constraints, liquidity, taxes, transaction costs, management fees, etc., and (iii) need for high computation power to determine the right distribution of selection in a timely bound manner.
The challenge in the MV model arises when it tries to compute covariance and hence cannot be employed in large scale portfolio optimization problems.

VaR Jorion (2007) could be misleading at times as it does not consider the worst case loss and cannot be applied in large portfolios. VaR Jorion (2007) is discrete in nature and difficult to simulate.

Both VaR Jorion (2007) and CVaR Rockafellar and Uryasev (2002) are efficient when the underlying risk factors are normally distributed, but face challenges for discrete distribution, making it non-convex
business_stakes: The paper says portfolio management matters because it helps organizations decide whether they will receive more or less investment and assess overall strategy and focus. It also notes that portfolio managers must account for transaction costs and that the employment of financial analysts including portfolio managers is expected to increase.
business_stakes_quotes: Proper analysis of portfolio can help a com- pany to analysis if the business would receive more or less investments. It also helps to analyze the overall strategy and focus of a company.

During the buying and selling of the assets, a transaction cost is imposed by the brokers or financial institutes as commission or other expenses Mansini et al. (2015). Henceforth, an optimum number of asset selection is important to reduce the transaction cost.
Also, as per the "Bureau of Labor Statistics", the employment of financial analyst including portfolio managers is expected to increase by 5% from 2019 to 2029.
extraction_notes: Review paper with explicit motivation in abstract/introduction; framing is broad but clearly financial.
